title: Ingles Markets sends a letter to shareholders amid its proxy fight
content:
[Professional office workers having a candid discussion in a boardroom]
Lisa5201/iStock via Getty Images

The board of directors of Ingles Markets (IMKTA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/IMKTA]) sent an open letter to shareholders related to its proxy fight. Ahead of the company's annual meeting on April 30, the company urged shareholders to vote for its two nominees, Rebekah Lowe and Dwight Jacobs. The board said the vote is critical because it is trying to block Rory Held, the nominee backed by Summer Road LLC, which Ingles (IMKTA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/IMKTA]) says is tied to the Sackler family and would create conflicted loyalties and value risk for the company.

In the letter, Ingles Markets (IMKTA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/IMKTA]) argued that it has been recovering well from Hurricane Helene and that its business momentum is improving. It pointed to stronger FQ1 results, including higher sales, same-store sales, gross profit, net income, and EBITDA. The balance sheet was said to remain strong. Ingles also says it believes its strategy of investing in stores, technology, equipment, real estate, and customer service has helped deliver strong long-term shareholder returns.

The company’s main objection to Held is not just that he would represent an activist investor, but that his ties to Sackler-controlled trusts and entities could create divided fiduciary duties. Ingles (IMKTA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/IMKTA]) argued that those ties would hurt customer trust, pharmacy sales, fuel sales, and ultimately the company’s reputation and long-term value. It also warned that Summer Road and Held are pushing a financial engineer agenda that stresses quick-hit gains at the expense of long-term value creation.

Shares of Ingles Markets (IMKTA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/IMKTA]) are up 47% over the last 52 weeks. Short interest on the grocery stock stands at 6.7% of the total float.

title: 3 Dividend Stocks That Are Obvious Buys in Today's Uncertain Market
content:
Uncertainty isn't just something you read about in headlines, you feel it when you open your portfolio and hesitate for a second longer than usual. When prices swing and narratives change every week, it forces a different kind of thinking.

You stop asking, "What could go up next?" and start asking, "What am I actually comfortable owning if things stay messy for a while?" Or even, "What am I OK with doubling down on?" That shift matters more than people realize. In calm markets, it's easy to convince yourself you're a long-term investor. But in volatile ones, you find out quickly if you really are, or whether you were just renting stocks that felt good at the time.

Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue »

I've found that the names you end up trusting most during those stretches tend to share a few traits: They're simple, they're consistent, and they return cash to you while you wait. Here are three that stand out right now, each for a different reason.Image source: Getty Images.

1. Weis Markets

Weis Markets (NYSE: WMK) operates about 200 grocery stores under its own banner, mostly in Pennsylvania and surrounding states. It's about as unglamorous as investing gets. But unexciting businesses in stable industries with consistent dividends are exactly what uncertain markets reward.

The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.34 per share in February 2026, yielding approximately 2% on an annualized basis. What's more interesting is the broader context. Some prominent investors have increased their stakes in Weis. The stock recently crossed below its 200-day moving average, a technical signal that has historically drawn value-oriented buyers.

Weis shares trade at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of roughly 15.6, below the broader consumer retailing industry average of 19.2. The company's domestic, regional supply chain means limited direct tariff exposure -- the vast majority of what Weis stores stock is sourced domestically. For an investor seeking a quiet, dividend-paying grocery stock that almost nobody is talking about, this is it.

2. Ingles Markets

Ingles Markets(NASDAQ: IMKTA) is a Southeast-focused supermarket chain headquartered in Asheville, North Carolina, operating hundreds of stores across the Carolinas, Georgia, Tennessee, Virginia, and Alabama. It also owns and operates its own milk and ice cream processing facility -- a level of vertical integration that most investors overlook. In March, Ingles declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.165 per share on its Class A shares.

Story Continues

There's also an activist shareholder situation developing, with investment firm Summer Road LLC challenging the board ahead of the April 30 shareholder meeting. Activism at a small, undervalued retailer is often a catalyst for unlocking value and, at minimum, means someone else is paying attention. Be wary here still. I would slowly invest as this challenge plays out.

3. Prestige Consumer Healthcare

Prestige Consumer Healthcare (NYSE: PBH) owns a portfolio of over-the-counter health and personal care brands -- Clear Eyes, Summer's Eve, Chloraseptic, Dramamine -- that people reach for when they're sick, uncomfortable, or not feeling their best. These aren't impulse purchases. They're need-based buys that hold up in an economic downturn.

In March, Prestige made its biggest move in years: It signed a definitive agreement to acquire the Breathe Right brand and several associated assets from Foundation Consumer Healthcare for $1.045 billion, or approximately $900 million net of an anticipated $150 million in tax benefits. The acquired portfolio generated about $200 million in trailing-12-month revenue. Breathe Right is expected to become Prestige's largest brand and give the company a new platform in the "better breathing" wellness category, with meaningful international reach.

Uncertainty doesn't make great businesses disappear. It just makes you more honest about what you actually trust. Weis Markets, Ingles Markets, and Prestige Consumer Healthcare each check different boxes, but they share the same core appeal: durability, cash flow, and relevance when conditions get tougher.

I'm not rushing in. Volatility and company-specific risks are still very real, but these are the kinds of names I'm comfortable watching closely and slowly building into if the market gives me the opportunity.

title: Stock Market Today, Feb. 12: AI Fears Slam Markets as Nasdaq Drops 2%
content:
Markets traded lower today as AI-related selling took its toll. The S&P 500(SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 1.57% to 6,832.76, the Nasdaq Composite(NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) dropped 2.03% to 22,597.15, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average(DJINDICES:^DJI) lost 1.34% to 49,451.98.

Market movers

Several high-profile tech names collapsed today on a mixture of AI angst and company-specific news. Cisco Systems(NASDAQ:CSCO)dropped 12.32% to $75.00 after disappointing forward revenue guidance. Palantir Technologies(NASDAQ:PLTR) fell following a bearish prediction from Michael Burry, made famous by the film The Big Short.

Supply chain and logistics player C.H. Robinson(NASDAQ:CHRW) tumbled 14.54% as AI replacement fears took hold. Defensive grocer Ingles Markets(NASDAQ:IMKTA) stood out as it notched a 52-week high.

What this means for investors

The AI apocalypse continues to pressure markets, with jitters spreading into any sector that could be unsettled by automation. That includes commercial real estate brokers, with CBRE Group(NYSE:CBRE) falling for the second day running on fears of AI disruption.

Today, Algorhythm Holdings(NASDAQ:RIME) said its AI tool could significantly scale freight volumes, prompting investors to pull away from transport and logistics firms. C.H. Robinson, Universal Logistics (NASDAQ:ULH), and RXO(NYSE:RXO) all plummeted.

There are some winners from the unfolding AI story. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) chip providers continue to gain. Micron(NASDAQ:MU), Sandisk(NASDAQ:SNDK), and Seagate Technology(NASDAQ:STX) were all in the green today.

Zooming out, yesterday’s strong jobs report put pay to hopes of Fed rate cuts in the coming months. There’s an expectation that tomorrow’s CPI release will show inflation is trending downwards.

title: Albertsons: Deep Value on the Surface, Opportunity Beneath?
content:
Albertsons Companies logo above fresh produce displays highlights consumer spending trends.

Key Points

Albertsons is recovering following the failed merger with Kroger, and it's trading at a deep value. The dividend is an added attraction, paying more than its peers, sustainably, with growth in the forecast. Institutional and analyst trends suggest this stock was accumulated in 2025 as its price fell, setting the stage for a robust rebound. Interested in Albertsons Companies, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Albertsons Companies (NYSE: ACI) presents a compelling value proposition in 2026, but the question is whether it is an opportunity for investors, and the signs suggest it is. While price action is bearish, results are outperforming expectations, and stock accumulation is underway. The company’s Q3 earnings report highlights continued outperformance versus expectations, reinforcing the bullish case despite bearish price action.

It is only a matter of time before this stock price reconnects with reality, and when it does, the gains that follow could be explosive. Semi-explosive, at least.

→ Why Baidu’s Quiet Spin-Off Could Unlock a Major Re-Rating

This isn’t exactly a high-growth story. We’re talking about a value-and-yield combination that suggests a high double-digit total return by the end of 2026 and the potential for a sustained rally as growth is reinvigorated.

Albertsons Presents a Favorable Value-and-Yield Combination

On a value basis, Albertsons trades at only 8x its current-year earnings outlook and 6x the 2030 consensus forecast, a discount relative to its peers every way you look at it. There are not many publicly traded direct competitors; Kroger (NYSE: KR) is number one, and Albertsons is number two. Kroger, the larger of the two, trades at 12x this year’s earnings and 10x the 2030 consensus, suggesting a minimum 50% upside is possible for ACI stock. Other comparisons, including those with regional player Ingles Markets (NASDAQ: IMKTA) and big-box stores such as Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) and Costco (NASDAQ: COST), reveal even more favorable valuations.

→ 3 of the Most Important Charts to Watch Right Now

The dividend yield heightens the value. Albertsons pays a reliable 60 cents as of early 2026, yielding approximately 3.5%, compared to a competitor range that tops out under 3%. The highest-yielding competitor is regional grocer Village Super Markets; the critical comparison is to Kroger, which yields about 2.25% with a similar payout ratio. Albertsons' dividend payout is under 30% of the fiscal year 2025 (FY2025) earnings consensus, according to MarketBeat, and the company has exceeded its targets every quarter so far.

Story Continues

Value and yield are among the reasons why the institutions accumulated in 2025. The data reveals mixed activity in Q4, with selling outpacing buying ever so slightly, but bullish behavior for the year. Institutions bought on balance each quarter at a pace of approximately $3 for each $1 sold and are likely to continue accumulating in 2026. The forecast is for this company to sustain its modest growth pace and to widen margins.

→ Rocket Lab’s Rally Isn’t Random—Big Catalysts Are Ahead

Tepid Guidance Sends ACI Shares to New Lows

Albertsons' Q4 FY2025 guidance fell short of the consensus, sending shares to new lows. However, the guidance adjustment merely narrowed the range, forecasting a mid-point slightly below the consensus. The takeaway is that growth is expected, including earnings, sustaining the capital return outlook. Data in the report also reveals strengths, including in comparable sales, digital channels, and loyalty, which underpin growth across the retail universe. The likely outcome is that Q4 guidance is cautious, and that a catalyst for a rebound may emerge before mid-year.

Catalysts in 2026 include the company’s strategic shift, increased loyalty engagement, and improved clarity now that the Kroger merger issues are behind it. The strategic shift focuses on digital, specifically its retail media network, which helps the grocery company leverage its growing loyalty base. The retail media network enables the company to sell ad space on its websites and apps, targeting specific shoppers and is a higher-margin business.

Albertsons Stock Overextends After Q3 Release

Albertsons' stock price has been under pressure for many quarters and is overextended in early 2026. Both the MACD and stochastic indicators reflect significant divergences, suggesting that a lack of buyers, rather than a dearth of sellers, is driving the market. In this scenario, the stock price is set up to rebound sharply and could do so at any time. The risk is that ACI stock will continue to drift lower until later in the year when more news is available. In that scenario, it could move to the post-IPO lows near $14 before rebounding.Albertsons stock chart shows technical divergences and falling price trend, signaling ACI may be overextended after recent sell-off.

title: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI): A Bull Case Theory
content:
We came across a bullish thesis on United Natural Foods, Inc. on The Value Road’s Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls’ thesis on UNFI. United Natural Foods, Inc.'s share was trading at $35.95 as of December 2nd. UNFI’s trailing and forward P/E were 9.45 and 17.64 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI), a major food distributor serving retailers like Whole Foods, experienced significant volatility over the past year. The company’s share price surged after implementing its “Simplified Supplier Agreement,” a new policy that effectively increased fees for suppliers using UNFI’s distribution network. This move initially boosted profitability and market sentiment, signaling improved operating leverage within its complex supply chain. However, the momentum was abruptly disrupted when UNFI fell victim to a large-scale cyberattack that temporarily crippled operations and led to widespread product shortages across key customers, including Whole Foods.

The incident triggered sharp selling pressure and sent the stock plummeting as investors questioned the company’s resilience and cybersecurity readiness. In the aftermath, UNFI responded swiftly, restoring operations, reinforcing its digital infrastructure, and resuming its strategic initiatives focused on efficiency and cost discipline. The company continued executing its long-term plan to rationalize its logistics footprint by closing redundant distribution centers and optimizing delivery routes, actions that are expected to enhance margins and strengthen free cash flow generation.

As operational stability returned, investor confidence gradually improved, driving a recovery in the stock price. Despite the earlier setbacks, UNFI’s streamlined structure, strengthened supplier relationships, and emphasis on operational efficiency position it to navigate a competitive distribution landscape more effectively. With key disruptions now resolved and ongoing improvements in execution, the company appears well-placed to deliver sustainable performance, making the current setup attractive for investors who believe in its continued turnaround potential and margin expansion story.

Previously we covered a bullish thesis on Ingles Markets, Incorporated (IMKTA) by Peter Thomason in May 2025, which highlighted the company’s undervalued real estate assets, consistent profitability, and owner-operator structure driving long-term compounding. The company’s stock price has appreciated by 24.73% since our coverage as the thesis played out. The thesis still stands as Ingles remains fundamentally strong.
